_meta._source: OCA Music Department engraved choir editions, as photocopied into the St John of Damascus (Tyler) service packets
_meta._note: PARISH-KEYED BY NECESSITY, NOT BY NATURE. The CONTENT is an OCA edition, not a parish text, and the project convention is to name a source set for its SOURCE. resolveOctoechos() walks the stack extends chain, so an edition-named file (octoechos-oca-music.json) would need a new translation layer inserted into Tyler extends_chain — which also re-orders the FIXED-TEXT cascade that dmitri-royster-overlay.test.js pins. Keyed to the parish id for now because that id is already in the chain and this changes nothing else. Migration to an edition-named layer is a follow-up.
_meta._arrayReplaceWarning: deepMergeOverlay REPLACES an array wholesale (server-lib/overlays/cascade.js:13). Every hymn of a section must be listed here, not just the changed ones. A one-element probe collapsed this aposticha from four hymns to one, and put it in the idiomelon slot.
_meta._transcription: Read VISUALLY from docs/choir-packets/2026-11-04/pdf/great-vespers-2026-11-07.pdf pp.2-3 (Lord I Call) and pp.9-10 (Aposticha) ("GREAT VESPERS / APOSTIKHA / RESURRECTION STICHERA / TONE 6"), not from the OCR sidecar. Nothing on those two pages is struck through, so all four are appointed. Capitalization and punctuation are AS PRINTED, including the source own lowercase divine pronouns; order 1 is transcribed too although its words already match the base, so the section reads from one source rather than two. The sheet "//" final-phrase break is stored as the newline this file uses throughout. Singer underlay marks are melodic, not textual, and are not transcribed.
_meta._familyNote: OCA. The OCA Music Department engraved choir editions — a different OCA EDITION from the service-texts DOCX that feeds the base, not a different translator. Declared explicitly rather than inferred from the prose _source, because prose inference is what laundered the HTM Beatitudes into the OCA family.
_meta._sourceTypos: Transcribed AS PRINTED, including two oddities of the director's sheet that a silent correction would hide: p.2 sticheron (9) reads "for he hast granted joy to the world" ("hast" with "he"), and p.3 sticheron (5) capitalises "Granting" mid-sentence at a line break. The choir already sings from this sheet; normalising either would re-open the gap between our text and theirs, which is the whole point of this file. Flag them to the director rather than editing here.
_meta._licSelection: The packet prints SEVEN Tone 6 resurrectional stichera, pre-numbered 10,9,8,7,6,5,4 for a set where the Octoechos takes 10-4. They are a LIBRARY, not a rubric: on 2026-11-07 the director strikes (6) because the Menaion supplies six stichera, so the Octoechos keeps 10-7. This file carries all seven texts; WHICH are sung stays entirely with the assembler, untouched. Packet 10..5 are base hymns 1..6; packet (4) is the separate "glory" node, the Resurrectional Doxastichon.
_meta._tone7Note: Tone 7 Lord-I-Call carries a SEVENTH resurrectional sticheron the base file lacks. reference/orders/2026-1115-order-services.txt appoints '7 stichera of the Resurrection, Tone 7'; the base holds 6, so licNoLeadingRepeat capped the ladder at 9 and every verse number sat one slot late (the packet's (10) was our v9). The seventh is transcribed AS PRINTED from docs/choir-packets/2026-11-11 great-vespers-2026-11-14.pdf p.3 position (4), read visually. It is in the MODERN register while the other six are thee/thou - the director sourced it outside OCA chant form, which is why the base never had it (see memory project_lic_seventh_resurrection_sticheron). Not added to the base: we cannot attribute it to OCA.

hymns.label: Idiomelon
hymns.text:
Thy resurrection, O Christ our Savior, the angels in heaven sing. Enable us on earth
to glorify thee in purity of heart.

hymns.label: Sticheron 2
hymns.text:
Destroying the gates of Hades; breaking the chains of death; Thou hast resurrected the fallen human race as almighty God.
O Lord, who rose from the dead: glory to thee.

hymns.label: Sticheron 3
hymns.text:
Desiring to return us to paradise, Christ was nailed to the cross and placed in a tomb. The myrrh-bearing women sought him with tears, crying out: woe to us, O savior. How dost thou deign to descend to death? What place can hold thy life bearing body? Come to us as thou hast promised. Take away our wailing and tears. Then the angel appeared to them: stop your lamentations. Go, proclaim to the apostles: the Lord is risen,
granting the world purification and great mercy.

hymns.label: Sticheron 4
hymns.text:
Having been crucified as thou didst will, by thy burial thou hast captured death, O Christ, and arose on the third day as God in glory,
granting the world unending life and great mercy.

resurrectional.note: Resurrectional stichera as the parish sings them — OCA Music Department engraved choir edition, NOT the OCA Obikhod (TT) wording of the base file.

hymns.text:
Possessing victory over Hades, O Christ, since thou art free among the dead, Thou didst ascend the cross raising with thyself those who sat in the shades of death. Drawing life from thine own light, O almighty savior,
have mercy on us.

Today Christ tramples on death, for he is risen as he said. Let us all sing this song, for he hast granted joy to the world: O light unapproachable, O fountain of life.
O Savior almighty: have mercy on us.

Where shall we sinners flee for thou art in all creation? In heaven thou dwellest; in Hades thou didst trample down death. In the depths of the sea? Even there is thy hand, O Master. To thee we flee, and falling before thee, we pray:
as thou didst rise from the dead, have mercy on us.

In thy cross, we glory, O Christ. We sing and glorify thy resurrection. For thou art our God,
and we know no other beside thee.

We bless the Lord by singing of his resurrection. For he endured the cross,
trampling down death by death.

Glory to thy might, O Lord, for thou hast overthrown the prince of death. By thy cross renewing us,
Granting us life and incorruption.

glory.text:
Thy burial destroyed the bonds of Hades, O Lord. Thy resurrection from the dead enlightened the world,
O Lord: glory to thee.

resurrectional.note: All SEVEN Tone 7 resurrectional stichera, as the parish sings them. Orders 1-6 are the OCA Obikhod text, verbatim from the base file and verified against the packet; order 7 is the one the base does not hold.

hymns.text:
Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, Who destroyed the dominion of death! Let us sing to Him with the bodiless hosts, for He enlightened the race of man!
O our Maker and Savior, glory to Thee!

Thou didst endure the Cross and burial for our sake. By Thy death, Thou didst destroy death as God. We fall down before Thy Resurrection on the third day,
O Savior, glory to Thee!

When the Apostles beheld the Resurrection of the Maker, they were amazed and sang the angelic praise. This is the glory of the Church. This is the richness of the Kingdom.
O Lord, crucified for our sake, glory to Thee!

Thou wast held by lawless men, O Christ, but to me, Thou art God, and I am not ashamed. Thou wast smitten on the cheek, but I do not deny Thee. Thou wast nailed to the Cross and I do not conceal it, for I glory in Thy Resurrection: Thy death is my life.
O almighty Lord and Lover of man, glory to Thee!

Fulfilling the prophecy of David, Christ manifested His greatness in Zion to the disciples. He is praised and always glorified, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit. At first as the Word, He was bodiless, but then He took flesh and was slain for our sake.
He rose in power as the Lover of man!

Thou didst descend into hell as Thou didst will, O Christ, overthrowing death as God and rising on the third day as Master! With Thyself Thou didst raise Adam from the bonds of hell and from corruption!
Glory to Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of man!

You were placed in the tomb, O Lord, as one asleep. On the third day you rose in power, Raising Adam with yourself from the corruption of death
As the almighty one.
